4 5 # TileLang-Ascend 6 7 8 [![Ask DeepWiki](https://deepwiki.com/badge.svg)](https://deepwiki.com/tile-ai/tilelang-ascend) 9 10
11 12 Tile Language Ascend (**tilelang-ascend**) is a specialized variant of the tile-lang domain-specific language, specifically optimized for Huawei Ascend NPU (Neural Processing Unit) architecture. Built upon the foundation of tile-lang's Pythonic syntax and [TVM](https://tvm.apache.org/) compiler infrastructure, tilelang-ascend enables developers to efficiently create high-performance AI compute kernels tailored for Ascend processors, including operations like GEMM, vector operations, and attention mechanisms. Tilelang-ascend allows developers to focus on productivity without sacrificing the low-level optimizations necessary for state-of-the-art performance on the NPU. The compiler backend supports two technical routes: [Ascend C & PTO](https://github.com/tile-ai/tilelang-ascend/tree/ascendc_pto) and [AscendNPU IR](https://github.com/tile-ai/tilelang-ascend/tree/npuir). 13 14

A DSL for high-performance AI workloads on Ascend NPUs. 35 36 ## Programming Guide 37 For more instructions and tips on using TileLang-Ascend, please refer to the [TileLang-Ascend Programming Guide](./docs/TileLang-Ascend%20Programming%20Guide.md). 38 39 ## Lessons 40 41 Welcome to the TileLang-Ascend video course series. You can access all the lessons via the links below: 42 43 | Lesson | Topic | Video Link | 44 | :---: | :--- | :---: | 45 | **01** | Introduction to TileLang-Ascend Development Environment | [📺 Start learning](https://www.bilibili.com/video/BV1EdFVzpEbg/) | 46 | **02** | TileLang-Ascend Programming Fundamentals | [📺 Start learning](https://www.bilibili.com/video/BV1uvFLzyEZ3/) | 47 | **03** | TileLang-Ascend Developer Programming Model Deep Dive | [📺 Start learning](https://www.bilibili.com/video/BV1DoFzz2EHB/) | 48 | **04** | Getting Started with TileLang-Ascend Performance Tuning and Debugging Tools | [📺 Start learning](https://www.bilibili.com/video/BV1QdFzz7E5W/) | 49 | **05** | TileLang-Ascend Engineering Practice: Compilation, Integration, and Deployment | [📺 Start learning](https://www.bilibili.com/video/BV1bmFkzHEb6/) | 50 51 ## Tested Devices 52 Although tilelang-ascend aims to be portable across a range of Ascend devices, it has been specifically tested and validated on the following NPUs: A2 and A3. 53 54 ## OP Implementation Examples 55 **tilelang-ascend** provides the building blocks to implement a wide variety of operators on the NPU. 56 Some examples include: 57 58 - [Matrix Multiplication (GEMM)](./examples/gemm/) 59 - [Batch GEMM](./examples/batch_gemm/) 60 - [Elementwise Operations](./examples/elementwise/) 61 - [Flash Attention](./examples/flash_attention/) 62 - [Sparse Flash Attention](./examples/sparse_flash_attention/) 63 - [Linear Attention & RNN](./examples/linear_attention_and_rnn/) 64 - [Softmax](./examples/softmax/) 65 - [Normalization](./examples/normalization/) 66 - [Activation Functions](./examples/activation/) 67 - [Reduce](./examples/reduce/) 68 - [Sort](./examples/sort/) 69 - [Convolution](./examples/convolution/) 70 - [Cross Entropy Loss](./examples/cross_entropy_loss/) 71 - [Dispatch & Combine](./examples/dispatch_combine/) 72 73 Within the `examples` directory, you will also find additional complex kernels—such as [LightningIndexer](./examples/lightning_indexer/), [TopK Selector](./examples/topk_selector/), and [ACLGraph Integration](./examples/aclgraph/). More operators are continuously being added. 74 75 76 ## Installation 77 78 ### Environment Preparation 79 We assume you already have an ascend environment with CANN (at least [8.3.RC1](https://www.hiascend.com/developer/download/community/result?cann=8.3.RC1&product=1&model=30)) and torch-npu (at least 2.6.0.RC1) installed. Firstly, set cann environment variables. 80 81 ```bash 82 source {your-cann-installed-path}/ascend-toolkit/set_env.sh 83 ``` 84 85 ### TileLang-Ascend Installation 86 87 Here we provide two installation methods: installing from wheel package and compiling from source code. 88 89 #### Method 1: Install from Wheel Package (Recommended) 90 91 Download the pre-built wheel package and install it directly: 92 93 ```bash 94 # Set Ascend environment variable 95 export ASCEND_HOME_PATH=/usr/local/Ascend/ascend-toolkit/latest 96 97 # Install the wheel package 98 pip install tilelang-*.whl 99 ``` 100 101 #### Method 2: Build Wheel Package from Source 102 103 If you need to build the wheel package from source: 104 105 ```bash 106 # Clone the repository 107 git clone --recursive https://github.com/tile-ai/tilelang-ascend.git 108 cd tilelang-ascend 109 110 # Set Ascend environment variable 111 export ASCEND_HOME_PATH=/usr/local/Ascend/ascend-toolkit/latest 112 113 # Build and install wheel package 114 ./build_wheel_ascend.sh [--enable-llvm] 115 116 # Install the built wheel package 117 pip install dist/tilelang-*.whl 118 ``` 119 120 #### Method 3: Compile and Install from Source 121 122 a) Download 123 124 git clone --recursive https://github.com/tile-ai/tilelang-ascend.git 125 cd tilelang-ascend 126 127 b) Compile and Install 128 129 bash install_ascend.sh 130 131 c) Environment Variable Setup 132 133 source set_env.sh 134 135 ## Run 136 137 138 In this section, you will learn how to call NPU TileLang operators. 139 140 Here we use the **Matrix Multiplication** operator as an example for introduction. 141 142 143 ``` 144 cd examples/gemm 145 python example_gemm.py 146 ``` 147 148 Upon success, it will print: 149 150 ``` 151 Kernel Output Match! 152 ``` 153 154 ## Comparison with NVIDIA Backend Implementation 155 156 GPUs primarily feature a three-level memory hierarchy that can be analogously mapped to NPU hardware architecture as follows: 157 158 **Memory Hierarchy Mapping:** 159 - `global memory` ↔ `global memory` 160 - `shared memory` ↔ `L1 buffer on cube core and unified buffer on vector core` 161 - `register memory` ↔ `L0A/B/C buffer` 162 163 **Memory Management:** 164 TileLang-Ascend provides memory allocation primitives similar to the GPU version. For example, `alloc_{L1/ub/...}` functions allow on-chip memory allocation in a manner comparable to GPU programming. 165 166 **Multiple Styles for Vector Operations:** 167 TileLang-Ascend offers multiple ways to express vector computations on the NPU, from high-level automatic vectorization to fine-grained tile primitives: 168 169 ```python 170 # Style 1: T.Parallel — automatic vectorization 171 for (i, j) in T.Parallel(M, N): 172 C_ub[i, j] = A_ub[i, j] + B_ub[i, j] 173 174 # Style 2: Tile primitives — explicit tile-level operations 175 T.tile.add(C_ub, A_ub, B_ub) 176 ``` 177 178 **Automatic Cube/Vector Scope Separation:** 179 Cube and vector cores on A2/A3 exchange data through global memory/L2 cache. In **Developer mode**, the compiler automatically separates Cube/Vector scopes and inserts synchronization. In **Expert mode**, you explicitly specify execution scopes using `T.Scope("C")/T.Scope("V")` and manage synchronization via `T.set_cross_flag` / `T.wait_cross_flag`. 180 181 182 ## Quick Start 183 184 In this section, you'll learn how to write and execute a straightforward GEMM (matrix multiplication) kernel using tilelang-ascend, The next chapter will introduce how to write a high-performance gemm kernel. 185 186 ### GEMM Example with Annotations 187 188 Below is an example that demonstrates how to quickly implement a gemm on the ascend. 189 190 ```python 191 @tilelang.jit(out_idx=[-1]) 192 def matmul(M, N, K, block_M, block_N, K_L1, dtype="float16", accum_dtype="float"): 193 194 # Calculate number of blocks in M and N dimensions 195 m_num = M // block_M 196 n_num = N // block_N 197 198 @T.prim_func 199 def main( 200 A: T.Tensor((M, K), dtype), # Input matrix A (M×K) 201 B: T.Tensor((K, N), dtype), # Input matrix B (K×N) 202 C: T.Tensor((M, N), dtype), # Output matrix C (M×N) 203 ): 204 205 with T.Kernel(m_num * n_num, is_npu=True) as (cid, _): 206 207 bx = cid // n_num # Block row index 208 by = cid % n_num # Block column index 209 210 # Allocate L1 cache buffers for input matrices 211 A_L1 = T.alloc_L1((block_M, K_L1), dtype) # A block in L1 212 B_L1 = T.alloc_L1((K_L1, block_N), dtype) # B block in L1 213 214 # Allocate L0C buffer for accumulation 215 C_L0 = T.alloc_L0C((block_M, block_N), accum_dtype) 216 217 # Core computation scope 218 with T.Scope("C"): 219 # Calculate number of K-dimension iterations 220 loop_k = T.ceildiv(K, K_L1) 221 222 # Iterate over K dimension blocks 223 for k in T.serial(loop_k): 224 # Copy A and B blocks from global memory to L1 cache 225 T.copy(A[bx * block_M, k * K_L1], A_L1) 226 T.copy(B[k * K_L1, by * block_N], B_L1) 227 228 # Synchronize all cores before computation 229 T.barrier_all() 230 231 # Perform matrix multiplication 232 T.gemm_v0(A_L1, B_L1, C_L0, init=(k == 0)) 233 234 # Synchronize all cores after computation 235 T.barrier_all() 236 237 # Copy final result from L0C to global memory 238 T.copy(C_L0, C[bx * block_M, by * block_N]) 239 240 return main 241 ``` 242 243 ### High Performance GEMM Example. (Layout, L2 Cache Swizzling, and Pipelining, etc.) 244 245 Below is an example that demonstrates more advanced features: layout annotation, parallelized copy, and swizzle for improved L2 cache locality. This snippet shows how to adapt your kernel to maximize performance on complex hardware. 246 247 ```python 248 @tilelang.jit(out_idx=[-1]) 249 def matmul(M, N, K, block_M, block_N, block_K, K_L1, S1, S2, dtype="float16", accum_dtype="float"): 250 m_num = M // block_M 251 n_num = N // block_N 252 253 core_num = 20 254 255 @T.macro 256 def init_flag(): 257 T.set_flag("mte1", "mte2", 0) 258 T.set_flag("mte1", "mte2", 1) 259 T.set_flag("m", "mte1", 0) 260 T.set_flag("m", "mte1", 1) 261 T.set_flag("fix", "m", 0) 262 263 @T.macro 264 def clear_flag(): 265 T.wait_flag("mte1", "mte2", 0) 266 T.wait_flag("mte1", "mte2", 1) 267 T.wait_flag("m", "mte1", 0) 268 T.wait_flag("m", "mte1", 1) 269 T.wait_flag("fix", "m", 0) 270 271 @T.prim_func 272 def main( 273 A: T.Tensor((M, K), dtype), 274 B: T.Tensor((K, N), dtype), 275 C: T.Tensor((M, N), dtype), 276 ): 277 with T.Kernel(core_num, is_npu=True) as (cid, _): 278 A_L1 = T.alloc_L1((S1, block_M, K_L1), dtype) 279 B_L1 = T.alloc_L1((S1, K_L1, block_N), dtype) 280 281 T.annotate_layout({ 282 A_L1: make_zn_layout(A_L1), 283 B_L1: make_zn_layout(B_L1), 284 }) 285 286 A_L0 = T.alloc_L0A((S2, block_M, block_K), dtype) 287 B_L0 = T.alloc_L0B((S2, block_K, block_N), dtype) 288 C_L0 = T.alloc_L0C((block_M, block_N), accum_dtype) 289 290 with T.Scope("C"): 291 init_flag() 292 293 for i in T.serial(T.ceildiv(m_num * n_num, core_num)): 294 T.use_swizzle( 295 i * core_num + cid, M, N, K, block_M, block_N, off=3, in_loop=True) 296 bx = cid // n_num 297 by = cid % n_num 298 299 loop_k = T.ceildiv(K, K_L1) 300 301 T.wait_flag("mte1", "mte2", 0) 302 T.copy(A[bx * block_M, 0], A_L1[0, :, :]) 303 T.copy(B[0, by * block_N], B_L1[0, :, :]) 304 T.set_flag("mte2", "mte1", 0) 305 T.wait_flag("fix", "m", 0) 306 for k in T.serial(loop_k): 307 if k < loop_k - 1: 308 T.wait_flag("mte1", "mte2", (k + 1) % S1) 309 T.copy(A[bx * block_M, (k + 1) * K_L1], A_L1[(k + 1) % S1, :, :]) 310 T.copy(B[(k + 1) * K_L1, by * block_N], B_L1[(k + 1) % S1, :, :]) 311 T.set_flag("mte2", "mte1", (k + 1) % S1) 312 313 loop_kk = T.ceildiv(K_L1, block_K) 314 315 for kk in T.serial(loop_kk): 316 if kk == 0: 317 T.wait_flag("mte2", "mte1", k % S1) 318 T.wait_flag("m", "mte1", kk % S2) 319 T.copy(A_L1[k % S1, 0, kk * block_K], A_L0[kk % S2, :, :]) 320 T.copy(B_L1[k % S1, kk * block_K, 0], B_L0[kk % S2, :, :]) 321 if kk == 3: 322 T.set_flag("mte1", "mte2", k % S1) 323 T.set_flag("mte1", "m", kk % S2) 324 T.wait_flag("mte1", "m", kk % S2) 325 326 if k == 0 and kk == 0: 327 T.mma(A_L0[kk % S2, :, :], B_L0[kk % S2, :, :], C_L0, init=True) 328 else: 329 T.mma(A_L0[kk % S2, :, :], B_L0[kk % S2, :, :], C_L0) 330 331 T.set_flag("m", "mte1", kk % S2) 332 333 T.set_flag("m", "fix", 0) 334 T.wait_flag("m", "fix", 0) 335 T.copy(C_L0, C[bx * block_M, by * block_N]) 336 T.set_flag("fix", "m", 0) 337 338 clear_flag() 339 340 T.barrier_all() 341 342 return main 343 ``` 344 345 ### Automatic insertion of synchronization instruction 346 347 We have supported automatic insertion of synchronization instructions within the core, which can be enabled by setting the TL_ASCEND_AUTO_SYNC attribute in the JIT's pass_configs parameter. Here is a simple example: 348 349 ```python 350 pass_configs = { 351 tilelang.PassConfigKey.TL_ASCEND_AUTO_SYNC: True 352 } 353 @tilelang.jit(out_idx=[-1], pass_configs=pass_configs) 354 def vec_add(M, N, block_M, block_N, dtype="float"): 355 m_num = M // block_M 356 n_num = N // block_N 357 358 VEC_NUM = 2 359 360 @T.prim_func 361 def main( 362 A: T.Tensor((M, N), dtype), 363 B: T.Tensor((M, N), dtype), 364 C: T.Tensor((M, N), dtype), 365 ): 366 # Enable by setting the enable_auto_sync attribute 367 T.func_attr({"enable_auto_sync": True}) 368 with T.Kernel(m_num * n_num, is_npu=True) as (cid, vid): 369 bx = cid // n_num 370 by = cid % n_num 371 372 a_ub = T.alloc_ub((block_M // VEC_NUM, block_N), dtype) 373 b_ub = T.alloc_ub((block_M // VEC_NUM, block_N), dtype) 374 c_ub = T.alloc_ub((block_M // VEC_NUM, block_N), dtype) 375 with T.Scope("V"): 376 T.copy(A[bx * block_M + vid * block_M // VEC_NUM, by * block_N], a_ub) 377 T.copy(B[bx * block_M + vid * block_M // VEC_NUM, by * block_N], b_ub) 378 379 T.add(c_ub, a_ub, b_ub) 380 381 T.copy(c_ub, C[bx * block_M + vid * block_M // VEC_NUM, by * block_N]) 382 383 return main 384 ``` 385 386 ### Automatic Buffer Reuse 387 388 We have supported automatic buffer reuse, which can be enabled by setting the TL_ASCEND_MEMORY_PLANNING attribute in the JIT's pass_configs parameter. Here is a example based on example_sparse_flash_attn.py: 389 390 ```python 391 pass_configs = { 392 tilelang.PassConfigKey.TL_ASCEND_MEMORY_PLANNING: True 393 } 394 @tilelang.jit(out_idx=[3], pass_configs=pass_configs) 395 def sparse_attention_fwd( 396 # other code... 397 398 #Manual configuration of T.annotate_address is no longer needed. 399 400 # T.annotate_address({ 401 # # L1 address 402 # q_l1: 0, 403 # q_tail_l1: 65536, 404 # kv_l1: 73728, 405 # kv_tail_l1: 139264, 406 # acc_s_l1: 139264, 407 408 # # L0C address 409 # acc_s_l0c: 0, 410 # acc_o_l0c: 0, 411 412 # ## ub address 413 # acc_o: 0, 414 # sumexp: 65536, 415 # m_i: 65664, 416 # indices_ub_: 65792, 417 # kv_ub: 66048, 418 # kv_tail_ub: 67072, 419 # acc_s_ub: 66048, 420 # m_i_prev: 74240, 421 # acc_s_ub_: 74368, 422 # tmp_ub: 74368, 423 # sumexp_i_ub: 98944, 424 # acc_s_half: 98944, 425 # acc_o_ub: 98944, 426 # acc_o_half: 98944 427 # }) 428 429 # other code... 430 ) 431 ``` 432 ### T.Parallel 433 We have supported [T.parallel](https://github.com/tile-ai/tilelang-ascend/blob/ascendc_pto/docs/tutorials/t_parallel.md), which transforms the parallel iteration space into vectorized operations that are lowered into AscendC vector instructions. Here is an example based on [example_sparse_flash_attn.py](https://github.com/tile-ai/tilelang-ascend/blob/ascendc_pto/examples/sparse_flash_attention/example_sparse_flash_attn.py): 434 435 ```python 436 pass_configs = { 437 tilelang.PassConfigKey.TL_ASCEND_AUTO_SYNC: True 438 } 439 @tilelang.jit(out_idx=[3], pass_configs=pass_configs) 440 def sparse_attention_fwd( 441 ... 442 # T.tile.add(acc_s_ub, acc_s_ub, acc_s_ub_) 443 for (i, j) in T.Parallel(v_block, BI): 444 acc_s_ub[i, j] = acc_s_ub[i, j] + acc_s_ub_[i, j] 445 ... 446 447 # T.tile.mul(acc_s_ub, acc_s_ub, sm_scale) 448 for (i, j) in T.Parallel(v_block, BI): 449 acc_s_ub[i, j] = acc_s_ub[i, j] * sm_scale 450 ... 451 452 # T.tile.max(m_i, m_i, m_i_prev) 453 for i in T.Parallel(v_block): 454 m_i[i] = T.max(m_i[i], m_i_prev[i]) 455 ... 456 457 # for h_i in range(v_block): 458 # T.tile.sub(acc_s_ub[h_i, :], acc_s_ub[h_i, :], m_i[h_i]) 459 for (h_i, j) in T.Parallel(v_block, D): 460 acc_s_ub[h_i, j] = acc_s_ub[h_i, j] - m_i[h_i] 461 ) 462 ``` 463 464 ### Auto-allocated Workspace 465 We now support [automatic workspace allocation](./docs/tutorials/automatic_workspace_allocation.md), enabling users to call operators without managing workspace or output tensor allocation—they only need to handle input tensors. Refer to [example_sparse_flash_attn.py](https://github.com/tile-ai/tilelang-ascend/blob/ascendc_pto/examples/sparse_flash_attention/example_sparse_flash_attn.py) for a concrete example. 466 ```python 467 # Specify workspace positions in parameter list via workspace_idx 468 @tilelang.jit(out_idx=[3], workspace_idx=[4,5,6,7,8]) 469 def sparse_attention_fwd(...): 470 @T.prim_func 471 def main( 472 # --- Input tensors --- 473 Q: T.Tensor(q_shape, dtype), 474 KV: T.Tensor(kv_shape, dtype), 475 Indices: T.Tensor(indices_shape, indices_dtype), 476 477 # --- Auto-allocated output (index 3 in out_idx) --- 478 Output: T.Tensor(o_shape, dtype), 479 480 # --- Auto-allocated workspaces (indices 4-8 in workspace_idx) --- 481 # These are temporary buffers managed by the runtime 482 workspace_1: T.Tensor([block_num, BI, D], dtype), 483 workspace_2: T.Tensor([block_num, BI, D_tail], dtype), 484 workspace_3: T.Tensor([block_num, H_per_block, BI], accum_dtype), 485 workspace_4: T.Tensor([block_num, H_per_block, BI], dtype), 486 workspace_5: T.Tensor([block_num, H_per_block, D], accum_dtype), 487 ): 488 489 ... 490 491 # Instantiate sparse attention function 492 func = sparse_attention_fwd( 493 heads=128, 494 dim=512, 495 tail_dim=64, 496 topk=2048, 497 kv_stride=1, 498 ) 499 500 # Prepare input tensors 501 q = torch.randn((B, S, H, DQK), dtype=dtype) 502 kv = torch.randn((B, SKV, HKV, DQK), dtype=dtype) 503 indices = torch.full((B, S, HKV, topk), SKV, dtype=torch.int32) 504 for b in range(B): 505 for t in range(S): 506 for h in range(HKV): 507 i_i = torch.randperm(max(1, ((t + q_start_s_index) // KV_stride)))[:topk] 508 indices[b, t, h, :len(i_i)] = i_i 509 510 # Call operator - output and workspaces are automatically allocated! 511 output = func(q, kv, indices) 512 ``` 513 ### T.Pipelined 514 [T.Pipelined](https://github.com/tile-ai/tilelang-ascend/blob/ascendc_pto/docs/tutorials/t_pipelined.md) enables automatic pipeline scheduling to achieve intra-core computation and data movement overlap, as well as inter-core pipeline overlap between Cube and Vector units. 515 516 **Usage:** 517 ```python 518 for i in T.Pipelined(loop_range, num_stages=N): 519 # loop body 520 ``` 521 522 **Usage Constraints:** 523 - `T.Pipelined` **does not support nesting**. You cannot place a `T.Pipelined` loop inside another `T.Pipelined` loop. 524 - For inter-core pipelining, place both Cube and Vector operations in a single `T.Pipelined` loop. 525 - For intra-core pipelining only, use separate `T.Pipelined` loops for Cube and Vector respectively. 526 527 ```python 528 # Correct: inter-core pipeline (Cube + Vector in one loop) 529 for i in T.Pipelined(loop, num_stages=2): 530 cube_operations() 531 vector_operations() 532 533 # Correct: intra-core pipeline (separate loops) 534 for i in T.Pipelined(loop, num_stages=2): 535 cube_operations() 536 for i in T.Pipelined(loop, num_stages=2): 537 vector_operations() 538 539 # WRONG: nested T.Pipelined is NOT supported 540 for i in T.Pipelined(outer, num_stages=2): 541 for j in T.Pipelined(inner, num_stages=2): # Error! 542 ... 543 ``` 544 545 An intra-core example refers to [matmul_add_pipeline.py](https://github.com/tile-ai/tilelang-ascend/blob/ascendc_pto/examples/pipeline/matmul_add_pipeline.py): 546 ```python 547 for k in T.Pipelined(loop_k, num_stages=2): 548 T.copy(A[bx * block_M, k * block_K], A_L1) 549 T.copy(B[k * block_K, by * block_N], B_L1) 550 551 T.barrier_all() 552 if k == 0: 553 T.gemm_v0(A_L1, B_L1, C_L0, init=True) 554 else: 555 T.gemm_v0(A_L1, B_L1, C_L0) 556 557 T.barrier_all() 558 ``` 559 560 An inter-core example refers to [flash_attn_bshd_pipeline.py](https://github.com/tile-ai/tilelang-ascend/blob/ascendc_pto/examples/pipeline/flash_attn_bshd_pipeline.py): 561 ```python 562 for k in T.Pipelined(T.ceildiv(seq_len, block_N), num_stages=2): 563 T.copy(K[bz, by, k * block_N:(k + 1) * block_N, :], k_l1) 564 T.gemm_v0(q_l1, k_l1, acc_s_l0c, transpose_B=True, init=True) 565 T.copy(acc_s_l0c, workspace_1[cid, :, :]) 566 567 T.tile.fill(acc_s_ub, 0.0) 568 T.copy(m_i, m_i_prev) 569 T.copy( 570 workspace_1[cid, vid * block_M // 2:vid * block_M // 2 + block_M // 2, :], 571 acc_s_ub_) 572 T.tile.add(acc_s_ub, acc_s_ub, acc_s_ub_) 573 T.tile.mul(acc_s_ub, acc_s_ub, sm_scale) 574 ... 575 ``` 576 577 For performance tuning with `T.Pipelined` (choosing `num_stages`, Double Buffer, etc.), see the [Flash Attention Performance Optimization Guide](./examples/flash_attention/fa_opt/flash_attention_performance_optimization_zh.md). 578 579 ### Dive Deep into TileLang Beyond GEMM 580 581 In addition to GEMM, we provide a variety of examples to showcase the versatility and power of TileLang-Ascend, including: 582 583 - [FlashAttention](./examples/flash_attention/): Implementations of FlashAttention with TileLang-Ascend. 584 - [LightningIndexer](./examples/lightning_indexer/): Implementations of LightningIndexer with TileLang-Ascend. 585 - [SparseFlashAttention](./examples/sparse_flash_attention/): Implementations of SparseFlashAttention with TileLang-Ascend. 586 587 ### Automatic insert synchronization flags between AIC and AIV, such as CrossCoreSetFlag / CrossCoreWaitFlag. 588 589 Two switches need to be turned on: 590 ```python 591 pass_configs = { 592 tilelang.PassConfigKey.TL_ASCEND_AUTO_CV_COMBINE: True, 593 tilelang.PassConfigKey.TL_ASCEND_AUTO_CV_SYNC: True, 594 } 595 ``` 596 597 Here is an example: 598 - [FlashAttention](./examples/flash_attention/flash_attn_bhsd_cc_sync.py): Implementations of FlashAttention without inserting synchronization flags manually. 599 600 ### Vid reduction & Auto CV Ratio 601 602 The parameter `threads` needs to be set. (Only 1 or 2 are allowed).When setting thread parameters, the return value will only have cid and no vid： 603 ```python 604 with T.Kernel(m_num * n_num, threads=2, is_npu=True) as (cid): 605 ``` 606 Therefore, ub application and transfer will no longer need to consider core allocation, and the usage will change as follows: 607 ```python 608 # UB allocation original form 609 c_ub = T.alloc_shared((block_M // VEC_NUM, block_N), dtype) 610 # New form after UB reduce elimination 611 c_ub = T.alloc_shared((block_M, block_N), dtype) 612 # UB moved to its original form 613 T.copy(c_ub, C[bx * block_M + vid * block_M // VEC_NUM, by * block_N]) 614 # New form after UB transport elimination 615 T.copy(c_ub, C[bx * block_M, by * block_N]) 616 # for loop original form 617 for h_i, j in T.Parallel(v_block // VEC_NUM, BI): 618 acc_s_ub[h_i, j] = acc_s_ub[h_i, j] - m_i[h_i] 619 # New form after UB transport elimination 620 for h_i, j in T.Parallel(v_block, BI): 621 acc_s_ub[h_i, j] = acc_s_ub[h_i, j] - m_i[h_i] 622 623 ``` 624 625 Here is some examples: 626 - [MatmulAddDeveloper](./examples/developer_mode/matmul_add_developer.py) 627 - [SparseFlashAttnDeveloperVidReduce](./examples/developer_mode/sparse_flash_attn_developer_vid_reduce.py) 628 629 For a more detailed feature introduction, please see: 630 - [vid_reduction_and_auto_cv_ratio.md](./docs/tutorials/vid_reduction_and_auto_cv_ratio.md) 631 632 ### Workspace reduction 633 634 Workspace Reduction is **automatically enabled** in the compilation pipeline. No manual configuration required. It automates workspace allocation for cross-core data transfer (L0C → UB), eliminating the need for users to manually write two-stage GM copy scripts and manage workspace buffers. 635 636 ```python 637 @T.prim_func 638 def flash_attn(...): 639 with T.Kernel(..., threads=2, is_npu=True) as (cid): 640 # Cube computation 641 T.gemm_v0(q_l1, k_l1, acc_s_l0c, transpose_B=True, init=True) 642 643 # Single copy statement — Workspace Reduction automatically handles GM transfer 644 T.copy(acc_s_l0c, acc_s_ub) 645 646 # Vector computation 647 T.tile.exp(acc_s_ub, acc_s_ub) 648 T.reduce_max(acc_s_ub, m_i, dim=-1) 649 T.tile.sub(acc_s_ub, acc_s_ub, m_i) 650 ``` 651 652 Here are some examples: 653 - [FlashAttnDeveloper](./examples/developer_mode/flash_attn_bshd_developer.py) 654 655 For a more detailed feature introduction, please see: 656 - [workspace_reduction_tutorial.md](./docs/tutorials/workspace_reduction_tutorial.md) 657 658 ## Contributing 659 660 We welcome contributions of new operators and framework improvements! Please follow the guidelines below to ensure your changes integrate smoothly. 661 662 ### Contributing Operators 663 664 When adding a new operator: 665 666 1. Create your operator under the `examples/` directory (e.g., `examples/my_op/my_op.py`). 667 2. Make sure your script prints `Kernel Output Match!` or `Test Passed!` upon success, so the CI can recognize it. 668 3. Verify that `bench_test.sh` can discover and run your script — it auto-discovers `*.py` files up to 2 levels deep under `examples/`. 669 4. Run the full test suite locally before submitting: 670 ```bash 671 cd examples 672 bash bench_test.sh 673 ``` 674 675 ### Contributing Framework Changes 676 677 When modifying the compiler, passes, or runtime: 678 679 1. Ensure **all existing tests pass** by running `bench_test.sh` end-to-end. Framework changes must not break any existing operator. 680 2. The CI will also run `pytest` on `testing/python/` — make sure those tests pass as well. 681 3. If your change adds a new API or primitive, add corresponding test coverage under `testing/python/` or a new example under `examples/`. 682 683 ### CI Overview 684 685 The current CI workflow is triggered manually via [`bench_test.sh`](./examples/bench_test.sh). 686 687 688 > **Rule of thumb**: If you add an operator, make sure `bench_test.sh` picks it up. If you change the framework, make sure `bench_test.sh` still reports 100% pass. 689 690 ## Upcoming Features 691 692 Check our [tilelang-ascend development plan](https://github.com/tile-ai/tilelang-ascend/issues/3) for upcoming features. 693 694 695 696 ## Acknowledgements 697 We gratefully acknowledge the valuable support provided by Huawei's HiSilicon, ICT, Compiler and Programming Language Lab and the Peking University Kunpeng & Ascend Center for Excellence in Science, Education, and Innovation. 698

# TileLang-Ascend [![Ask DeepWiki](https://deepwiki.com/badge.svg)](https://deepwiki.com/tile-ai/tilelang-ascend)
Tile Language Ascend (**tilelang-ascend**) is a specialized variant of the tile-lang domain-specific language, specifically optimized for Huawei Ascend NPU (Neural Processing Unit) architecture. Built upon the foundation of tile-lang's Pythonic syntax and [TVM](https://tvm.apache.org/) compiler infrastructure, tilelang-ascend enables developers to efficiently create high-performance AI compute kernels tailored for Ascend processors, including operations like GEMM, vector operations, and attention mechanisms. Tilelang-ascend allows developers to focus on productivity without sacrificing the low-level optimizations necessary for state-of-the-art performance on the NPU. The compiler backend supports two technical routes: [Ascend C & PTO](https://github.com/tile-ai/tilelang-ascend/tree/ascendc_pto) and [AscendNPU IR](https://github.com/tile-ai/tilelang-ascend/tree/npuir).

## Latest News - 04/24/2026 🚀: Released DeepSeek V4 kernels [DeepSeek-V4](./examples/deepseek_v4/) - 03/28/2026 🚀: Released high-performance [Flash Attention](./examples/flash_attention/) & [Sparse Flash Attention](./examples/sparse_flash_attention/) benchmark and optimization guide, see [PR#698](https://github.com/tile-ai/tilelang-ascend/pull/698) and [PR#665](https://github.com/tile-ai/tilelang-ascend/pull/665). - 03/16/2026 🚀: Introduced [wheel package installation](https://github.com/tile-ai/tilelang-ascend?tab=readme-ov-file#installation), enabling easy setup via `pip install`! - 03/12/2026 ✨: New [ACLGraph](./examples/aclgraph/) integration example for graph-level optimization on Ascend NPU. - 03/03/2026 ✨: Supported [shared memory (shmem) with put/get API](https://github.com/tile-ai/tilelang-ascend/pull/194) for inter-core communication. - 01/29/2026 📖: Published the [TileLang-Ascend Programming Guide](./docs/TileLang-Ascend%20Programming%20Guide.md) with comprehensive development tutorials. - 01/23/2026 🚀: Landed [PTO backend](https://github.com/tile-ai/tilelang-ascend/pull/341) as a new code generation target. - 01/21/2026 ✨: New [torch_tl_ascend](./examples/torch_tl_ascend/) PyTorch integration example for seamless NPU + PyTorch workflows, see [PR#292](https://github.com/tile-ai/tilelang-ascend/pull/292). - 01/15/2026 ✨: Introduced [T.Pipelined](https://github.com/tile-ai/tilelang-ascend/pull/274) for software pipelining on Ascend NPU. - 12/08/2025 ✨: Supported [T.Parallel](https://github.com/tile-ai/tilelang-ascend?tab=readme-ov-file#tparallel) for automatic vectorization, check out [PR#113](https://github.com/tile-ai/tilelang-ascend/pull/113) for details. - 11/25/2025 ✨: Enabled [automatic buffer reuse](https://github.com/tile-ai/tilelang-ascend?tab=readme-ov-file#automatic-buffer-reuse) to reduce on-chip memory footprint, see [PR#101](https://github.com/tile-ai/tilelang-ascend/pull/101). - 11/17/2025 🛠️: Shipped debug tools `T.printf` and `T.dump_tensor` for [printing and dumping](https://github.com/tile-ai/tilelang-ascend/tree/ascendc_pto/examples/print) device-side buffers. - 11/07/2025 ✨: Enabled [automatic intra-kernel synchronization insertion](https://github.com/tile-ai/tilelang-ascend?tab=readme-ov-file#automatic-insertion-of-synchronization-instruction), see [PR#74](https://github.com/tile-ai/tilelang-ascend/pull/74). - 10/28/2025 🚀: Optimized tl_templates performance and delivered a high-performance [GEMM kernel](https://github.com/tile-ai/tilelang-ascend/blob/ascendc_pto/examples/gemm/example_gemm_intrinsic.py). - 09/29/2025 🎉: tilelang-ascend is now open source! A DSL for high-performance AI workloads on Ascend NPUs. ## Programming Guide For more instructions and tips on using TileLang-Ascend, please refer to the [TileLang-Ascend Programming Guide](./docs/TileLang-Ascend%20Programming%20Guide.md). ## Lessons Welcome to the TileLang-Ascend video course series. You can access all the lessons via the links below: | Lesson | Topic | Video Link | | :---: | :--- | :---: | | **01** | Introduction to TileLang-Ascend Development Environment | [📺 Start learning](https://www.bilibili.com/video/BV1EdFVzpEbg/) | | **02** | TileLang-Ascend Programming Fundamentals | [📺 Start learning](https://www.bilibili.com/video/BV1uvFLzyEZ3/) | | **03** | TileLang-Ascend Developer Programming Model Deep Dive | [📺 Start learning](https://www.bilibili.com/video/BV1DoFzz2EHB/) | | **04** | Getting Started with TileLang-Ascend Performance Tuning and Debugging Tools | [📺 Start learning](https://www.bilibili.com/video/BV1QdFzz7E5W/) | | **05** | TileLang-Ascend Engineering Practice: Compilation, Integration, and Deployment | [📺 Start learning](https://www.bilibili.com/video/BV1bmFkzHEb6/) | ## Tested Devices Although tilelang-ascend aims to be portable across a range of Ascend devices, it has been specifically tested and validated on the following NPUs: A2 and A3. ## OP Implementation Examples **tilelang-ascend** provides the building blocks to implement a wide variety of operators on the NPU. Some examples include: - [Matrix Multiplication (GEMM)](./examples/gemm/) - [Batch GEMM](./examples/batch_gemm/) - [Elementwise Operations](./examples/elementwise/) - [Flash Attention](./examples/flash_attention/) - [Sparse Flash Attention](./examples/sparse_flash_attention/) - [Linear Attention & RNN](./examples/linear_attention_and_rnn/) - [Softmax](./examples/softmax/) - [Normalization](./examples/normalization/) - [Activation Functions](./examples/activation/) - [Reduce](./examples/reduce/) - [Sort](./examples/sort/) - [Convolution](./examples/convolution/) - [Cross Entropy Loss](./examples/cross_entropy_loss/) - [Dispatch & Combine](./examples/dispatch_combine/) Within the `examples` directory, you will also find additional complex kernels—such as [LightningIndexer](./examples/lightning_indexer/), [TopK Selector](./examples/topk_selector/), and [ACLGraph Integration](./examples/aclgraph/). More operators are continuously being added. ## Installation ### Environment Preparation We assume you already have an ascend environment with CANN (at least [8.3.RC1](https://www.hiascend.com/developer/download/community/result?cann=8.3.RC1&product=1&model=30)) and torch-npu (at least 2.6.0.RC1) installed. Firstly, set cann environment variables. ```bash source {your-cann-installed-path}/ascend-toolkit/set_env.sh ``` ### TileLang-Ascend Installation Here we provide two installation methods: installing from wheel package and compiling from source code. #### Method 1: Install from Wheel Package (Recommended) Download the pre-built wheel package and install it directly: ```bash # Set Ascend environment variable export ASCEND_HOME_PATH=/usr/local/Ascend/ascend-toolkit/latest # Install the wheel package pip install tilelang-*.whl ``` #### Method 2: Build Wheel Package from Source If you need to build the wheel package from source: ```bash # Clone the repository git clone --recursive https://github.com/tile-ai/tilelang-ascend.git cd tilelang-ascend # Set Ascend environment variable export ASCEND_HOME_PATH=/usr/local/Ascend/ascend-toolkit/latest # Build and install wheel package ./build_wheel_ascend.sh [--enable-llvm] # Install the built wheel package pip install dist/tilelang-*.whl ``` #### Method 3: Compile and Install from Source a) Download git clone --recursive https://github.com/tile-ai/tilelang-ascend.git cd tilelang-ascend b) Compile and Install bash install_ascend.sh c) Environment Variable Setup source set_env.sh ## Run In this section, you will learn how to call NPU TileLang operators. Here we use the **Matrix Multiplication** operator as an example for introduction. ``` cd examples/gemm python example_gemm.py ``` Upon success, it will print: ``` Kernel Output Match! ``` ## Comparison with NVIDIA Backend Implementation GPUs primarily feature a three-level memory hierarchy that can be analogously mapped to NPU hardware architecture as follows: **Memory Hierarchy Mapping:** - `global memory` ↔ `global memory` - `shared memory` ↔ `L1 buffer on cube core and unified buffer on vector core` - `register memory` ↔ `L0A/B/C buffer` **Memory Management:** TileLang-Ascend provides memory allocation primitives similar to the GPU version. For example, `alloc_{L1/ub/...}` functions allow on-chip memory allocation in a manner comparable to GPU programming. **Multiple Styles for Vector Operations:** TileLang-Ascend offers multiple ways to express vector computations on the NPU, from high-level automatic vectorization to fine-grained tile primitives: ```python # Style 1: T.Parallel — automatic vectorization for (i, j) in T.Parallel(M, N): C_ub[i, j] = A_ub[i, j] + B_ub[i, j] # Style 2: Tile primitives — explicit tile-level operations T.tile.add(C_ub, A_ub, B_ub) ``` **Automatic Cube/Vector Scope Separation:** Cube and vector cores on A2/A3 exchange data through global memory/L2 cache. In **Developer mode**, the compiler automatically separates Cube/Vector scopes and inserts synchronization. In **Expert mode**, you explicitly specify execution scopes using `T.Scope("C")/T.Scope("V")` and manage synchronization via `T.set_cross_flag` / `T.wait_cross_flag`. ## Quick Start In this section, you'll learn how to write and execute a straightforward GEMM (matrix multiplication) kernel using tilelang-ascend, The next chapter will introduce how to write a high-performance gemm kernel. ### GEMM Example with Annotations Below is an example that demonstrates how to quickly implement a gemm on the ascend. ```python @tilelang.jit(out_idx=[-1]) def matmul(M, N, K, block_M, block_N, K_L1, dtype="float16", accum_dtype="float"): # Calculate number of blocks in M and N dimensions m_num = M // block_M n_num = N // block_N @T.prim_func def main( A: T.Tensor((M, K), dtype), # Input matrix A (M×K) B: T.Tensor((K, N), dtype), # Input matrix B (K×N) C: T.Tensor((M, N), dtype), # Output matrix C (M×N) ): with T.Kernel(m_num * n_num, is_npu=True) as (cid, _): bx = cid // n_num # Block row index by = cid % n_num # Block column index # Allocate L1 cache buffers for input matrices A_L1 = T.alloc_L1((block_M, K_L1), dtype) # A block in L1 B_L1 = T.alloc_L1((K_L1, block_N), dtype) # B block in L1 # Allocate L0C buffer for accumulation C_L0 = T.alloc_L0C((block_M, block_N), accum_dtype) # Core computation scope with T.Scope("C"): # Calculate number of K-dimension iterations loop_k = T.ceildiv(K, K_L1) # Iterate over K dimension blocks for k in T.serial(loop_k): # Copy A and B blocks from global memory to L1 cache T.copy(A[bx * block_M, k * K_L1], A_L1) T.copy(B[k * K_L1, by * block_N], B_L1) # Synchronize all cores before computation T.barrier_all() # Perform matrix multiplication T.gemm_v0(A_L1, B_L1, C_L0, init=(k == 0)) # Synchronize all cores after computation T.barrier_all() # Copy final result from L0C to global memory T.copy(C_L0, C[bx * block_M, by * block_N]) return main ``` ### High Performance GEMM Example. (Layout, L2 Cache Swizzling, and Pipelining, etc.) Below is an example that demonstrates more advanced features: layout annotation, parallelized copy, and swizzle for improved L2 cache locality. This snippet shows how to adapt your kernel to maximize performance on complex hardware. ```python @tilelang.jit(out_idx=[-1]) def matmul(M, N, K, block_M, block_N, block_K, K_L1, S1, S2, dtype="float16", accum_dtype="float"): m_num = M // block_M n_num = N // block_N core_num = 20 @T.macro def init_flag(): T.set_flag("mte1", "mte2", 0) T.set_flag("mte1", "mte2", 1) T.set_flag("m", "mte1", 0) T.set_flag("m", "mte1", 1) T.set_flag("fix", "m", 0) @T.macro def clear_flag(): T.wait_flag("mte1", "mte2", 0) T.wait_flag("mte1", "mte2", 1) T.wait_flag("m", "mte1", 0) T.wait_flag("m", "mte1", 1) T.wait_flag("fix", "m", 0) @T.prim_func def main( A: T.Tensor((M, K), dtype), B: T.Tensor((K, N), dtype), C: T.Tensor((M, N), dtype), ): with T.Kernel(core_num, is_npu=True) as (cid, _): A_L1 = T.alloc_L1((S1, block_M, K_L1), dtype) B_L1 = T.alloc_L1((S1, K_L1, block_N), dtype) T.annotate_layout({ A_L1: make_zn_layout(A_L1), B_L1: make_zn_layout(B_L1), }) A_L0 = T.alloc_L0A((S2, block_M, block_K), dtype) B_L0 = T.alloc_L0B((S2, block_K, block_N), dtype) C_L0 = T.alloc_L0C((block_M, block_N), accum_dtype) with T.Scope("C"): init_flag() for i in T.serial(T.ceildiv(m_num * n_num, core_num)): T.use_swizzle( i * core_num + cid, M, N, K, block_M, block_N, off=3, in_loop=True) bx = cid // n_num by = cid % n_num loop_k = T.ceildiv(K, K_L1) T.wait_flag("mte1", "mte2", 0) T.copy(A[bx * block_M, 0], A_L1[0, :, :]) T.copy(B[0, by * block_N], B_L1[0, :, :]) T.set_flag("mte2", "mte1", 0) T.wait_flag("fix", "m", 0) for k in T.serial(loop_k): if k < loop_k - 1: T.wait_flag("mte1", "mte2", (k + 1) % S1) T.copy(A[bx * block_M, (k + 1) * K_L1], A_L1[(k + 1) % S1, :, :]) T.copy(B[(k + 1) * K_L1, by * block_N], B_L1[(k + 1) % S1, :, :]) T.set_flag("mte2", "mte1", (k + 1) % S1) loop_kk = T.ceildiv(K_L1, block_K) for kk in T.serial(loop_kk): if kk == 0: T.wait_flag("mte2", "mte1", k % S1) T.wait_flag("m", "mte1", kk % S2) T.copy(A_L1[k % S1, 0, kk * block_K], A_L0[kk % S2, :, :]) T.copy(B_L1[k % S1, kk * block_K, 0], B_L0[kk % S2, :, :]) if kk == 3: T.set_flag("mte1", "mte2", k % S1) T.set_flag("mte1", "m", kk % S2) T.wait_flag("mte1", "m", kk % S2) if k == 0 and kk == 0: T.mma(A_L0[kk % S2, :, :], B_L0[kk % S2, :, :], C_L0, init=True) else: T.mma(A_L0[kk % S2, :, :], B_L0[kk % S2, :, :], C_L0) T.set_flag("m", "mte1", kk % S2) T.set_flag("m", "fix", 0) T.wait_flag("m", "fix", 0) T.copy(C_L0, C[bx * block_M, by * block_N]) T.set_flag("fix", "m", 0) clear_flag() T.barrier_all() return main ``` ### Automatic insertion of synchronization instruction We have supported automatic insertion of synchronization instructions within the core, which can be enabled by setting the TL_ASCEND_AUTO_SYNC attribute in the JIT's pass_configs parameter. Here is a simple example: ```python pass_configs = { tilelang.PassConfigKey.TL_ASCEND_AUTO_SYNC: True } @tilelang.jit(out_idx=[-1], pass_configs=pass_configs) def vec_add(M, N, block_M, block_N, dtype="float"): m_num = M // block_M n_num = N // block_N VEC_NUM = 2 @T.prim_func def main( A: T.Tensor((M, N), dtype), B: T.Tensor((M, N), dtype), C: T.Tensor((M, N), dtype), ): # Enable by setting the enable_auto_sync attribute T.func_attr({"enable_auto_sync": True}) with T.Kernel(m_num * n_num, is_npu=True) as (cid, vid): bx = cid // n_num by = cid % n_num a_ub = T.alloc_ub((block_M // VEC_NUM, block_N), dtype) b_ub = T.alloc_ub((block_M // VEC_NUM, block_N), dtype) c_ub = T.alloc_ub((block_M // VEC_NUM, block_N), dtype) with T.Scope("V"): T.copy(A[bx * block_M + vid * block_M // VEC_NUM, by * block_N], a_ub) T.copy(B[bx * block_M + vid * block_M // VEC_NUM, by * block_N], b_ub) T.add(c_ub, a_ub, b_ub) T.copy(c_ub, C[bx * block_M + vid * block_M // VEC_NUM, by * block_N]) return main ``` ### Automatic Buffer Reuse We have supported automatic buffer reuse, which can be enabled by setting the TL_ASCEND_MEMORY_PLANNING attribute in the JIT's pass_configs parameter. Here is a example based on example_sparse_flash_attn.py: ```python pass_configs = { tilelang.PassConfigKey.TL_ASCEND_MEMORY_PLANNING: True } @tilelang.jit(out_idx=[3], pass_configs=pass_configs) def sparse_attention_fwd( # other code... #Manual configuration of T.annotate_address is no longer needed. # T.annotate_address({ # # L1 address # q_l1: 0, # q_tail_l1: 65536, # kv_l1: 73728, # kv_tail_l1: 139264, # acc_s_l1: 139264, # # L0C address # acc_s_l0c: 0, # acc_o_l0c: 0, # ## ub address # acc_o: 0, # sumexp: 65536, # m_i: 65664, # indices_ub_: 65792, # kv_ub: 66048, # kv_tail_ub: 67072, # acc_s_ub: 66048, # m_i_prev: 74240, # acc_s_ub_: 74368, # tmp_ub: 74368, # sumexp_i_ub: 98944, # acc_s_half: 98944, # acc_o_ub: 98944, # acc_o_half: 98944 # }) # other code... ) ``` ### T.Parallel We have supported [T.parallel](https://github.com/tile-ai/tilelang-ascend/blob/ascendc_pto/docs/tutorials/t_parallel.md), which transforms the parallel iteration space into vectorized operations that are lowered into AscendC vector instructions. Here is an example based on [example_sparse_flash_attn.py](https://github.com/tile-ai/tilelang-ascend/blob/ascendc_pto/examples/sparse_flash_attention/example_sparse_flash_attn.py): ```python pass_configs = { tilelang.PassConfigKey.TL_ASCEND_AUTO_SYNC: True } @tilelang.jit(out_idx=[3], pass_configs=pass_configs) def sparse_attention_fwd( ... # T.tile.add(acc_s_ub, acc_s_ub, acc_s_ub_) for (i, j) in T.Parallel(v_block, BI): acc_s_ub[i, j] = acc_s_ub[i, j] + acc_s_ub_[i, j] ... # T.tile.mul(acc_s_ub, acc_s_ub, sm_scale) for (i, j) in T.Parallel(v_block, BI): acc_s_ub[i, j] = acc_s_ub[i, j] * sm_scale ... # T.tile.max(m_i, m_i, m_i_prev) for i in T.Parallel(v_block): m_i[i] = T.max(m_i[i], m_i_prev[i]) ... # for h_i in range(v_block): # T.tile.sub(acc_s_ub[h_i, :], acc_s_ub[h_i, :], m_i[h_i]) for (h_i, j) in T.Parallel(v_block, D): acc_s_ub[h_i, j] = acc_s_ub[h_i, j] - m_i[h_i] ) ``` ### Auto-allocated Workspace We now support [automatic workspace allocation](./docs/tutorials/automatic_workspace_allocation.md), enabling users to call operators without managing workspace or output tensor allocation—they only need to handle input tensors. Refer to [example_sparse_flash_attn.py](https://github.com/tile-ai/tilelang-ascend/blob/ascendc_pto/examples/sparse_flash_attention/example_sparse_flash_attn.py) for a concrete example. ```python # Specify workspace positions in parameter list via workspace_idx @tilelang.jit(out_idx=[3], workspace_idx=[4,5,6,7,8]) def sparse_attention_fwd(...): @T.prim_func def main( # --- Input tensors --- Q: T.Tensor(q_shape, dtype), KV: T.Tensor(kv_shape, dtype), Indices: T.Tensor(indices_shape, indices_dtype), # --- Auto-allocated output (index 3 in out_idx) --- Output: T.Tensor(o_shape, dtype), # --- Auto-allocated workspaces (indices 4-8 in workspace_idx) --- # These are temporary buffers managed by the runtime workspace_1: T.Tensor([block_num, BI, D], dtype), workspace_2: T.Tensor([block_num, BI, D_tail], dtype), workspace_3: T.Tensor([block_num, H_per_block, BI], accum_dtype), workspace_4: T.Tensor([block_num, H_per_block, BI], dtype), workspace_5: T.Tensor([block_num, H_per_block, D], accum_dtype), ): ... # Instantiate sparse attention function func = sparse_attention_fwd( heads=128, dim=512, tail_dim=64, topk=2048, kv_stride=1, ) # Prepare input tensors q = torch.randn((B, S, H, DQK), dtype=dtype) kv = torch.randn((B, SKV, HKV, DQK), dtype=dtype) indices = torch.full((B, S, HKV, topk), SKV, dtype=torch.int32) for b in range(B): for t in range(S): for h in range(HKV): i_i = torch.randperm(max(1, ((t + q_start_s_index) // KV_stride)))[:topk] indices[b, t, h, :len(i_i)] = i_i # Call operator - output and workspaces are automatically allocated! output = func(q, kv, indices) ``` ### T.Pipelined [T.Pipelined](https://github.com/tile-ai/tilelang-ascend/blob/ascendc_pto/docs/tutorials/t_pipelined.md) enables automatic pipeline scheduling to achieve intra-core computation and data movement overlap, as well as inter-core pipeline overlap between Cube and Vector units. **Usage:** ```python for i in T.Pipelined(loop_range, num_stages=N): # loop body ``` **Usage Constraints:** - `T.Pipelined` **does not support nesting**. You cannot place a `T.Pipelined` loop inside another `T.Pipelined` loop. - For inter-core pipelining, place both Cube and Vector operations in a single `T.Pipelined` loop. - For intra-core pipelining only, use separate `T.Pipelined` loops for Cube and Vector respectively. ```python # Correct: inter-core pipeline (Cube + Vector in one loop) for i in T.Pipelined(loop, num_stages=2): cube_operations() vector_operations() # Correct: intra-core pipeline (separate loops) for i in T.Pipelined(loop, num_stages=2): cube_operations() for i in T.Pipelined(loop, num_stages=2): vector_operations() # WRONG: nested T.Pipelined is NOT supported for i in T.Pipelined(outer, num_stages=2): for j in T.Pipelined(inner, num_stages=2): # Error! ... ``` An intra-core example refers to [matmul_add_pipeline.py](https://github.com/tile-ai/tilelang-ascend/blob/ascendc_pto/examples/pipeline/matmul_add_pipeline.py): ```python for k in T.Pipelined(loop_k, num_stages=2): T.copy(A[bx * block_M, k * block_K], A_L1) T.copy(B[k * block_K, by * block_N], B_L1) T.barrier_all() if k == 0: T.gemm_v0(A_L1, B_L1, C_L0, init=True) else: T.gemm_v0(A_L1, B_L1, C_L0) T.barrier_all() ``` An inter-core example refers to [flash_attn_bshd_pipeline.py](https://github.com/tile-ai/tilelang-ascend/blob/ascendc_pto/examples/pipeline/flash_attn_bshd_pipeline.py): ```python for k in T.Pipelined(T.ceildiv(seq_len, block_N), num_stages=2): T.copy(K[bz, by, k * block_N:(k + 1) * block_N, :], k_l1) T.gemm_v0(q_l1, k_l1, acc_s_l0c, transpose_B=True, init=True) T.copy(acc_s_l0c, workspace_1[cid, :, :]) T.tile.fill(acc_s_ub, 0.0) T.copy(m_i, m_i_prev) T.copy( workspace_1[cid, vid * block_M // 2:vid * block_M // 2 + block_M // 2, :], acc_s_ub_) T.tile.add(acc_s_ub, acc_s_ub, acc_s_ub_) T.tile.mul(acc_s_ub, acc_s_ub, sm_scale) ... ``` For performance tuning with `T.Pipelined` (choosing `num_stages`, Double Buffer, etc.), see the [Flash Attention Performance Optimization Guide](./examples/flash_attention/fa_opt/flash_attention_performance_optimization_zh.md). ### Dive Deep into TileLang Beyond GEMM In addition to GEMM, we provide a variety of examples to showcase the versatility and power of TileLang-Ascend, including: - [FlashAttention](./examples/flash_attention/): Implementations of FlashAttention with TileLang-Ascend. - [LightningIndexer](./examples/lightning_indexer/): Implementations of LightningIndexer with TileLang-Ascend. - [SparseFlashAttention](./examples/sparse_flash_attention/): Implementations of SparseFlashAttention with TileLang-Ascend. ### Automatic insert synchronization flags between AIC and AIV, such as CrossCoreSetFlag / CrossCoreWaitFlag. Two switches need to be turned on: ```python pass_configs = { tilelang.PassConfigKey.TL_ASCEND_AUTO_CV_COMBINE: True, tilelang.PassConfigKey.TL_ASCEND_AUTO_CV_SYNC: True, } ``` Here is an example: - [FlashAttention](./examples/flash_attention/flash_attn_bhsd_cc_sync.py): Implementations of FlashAttention without inserting synchronization flags manually. ### Vid reduction & Auto CV Ratio The parameter `threads` needs to be set. (Only 1 or 2 are allowed).When setting thread parameters, the return value will only have cid and no vid： ```python with T.Kernel(m_num * n_num, threads=2, is_npu=True) as (cid): ``` Therefore, ub application and transfer will no longer need to consider core allocation, and the usage will change as follows: ```python # UB allocation original form c_ub = T.alloc_shared((block_M // VEC_NUM, block_N), dtype) # New form after UB reduce elimination c_ub = T.alloc_shared((block_M, block_N), dtype) # UB moved to its original form T.copy(c_ub, C[bx * block_M + vid * block_M // VEC_NUM, by * block_N]) # New form after UB transport elimination T.copy(c_ub, C[bx * block_M, by * block_N]) # for loop original form for h_i, j in T.Parallel(v_block // VEC_NUM, BI): acc_s_ub[h_i, j] = acc_s_ub[h_i, j] - m_i[h_i] # New form after UB transport elimination for h_i, j in T.Parallel(v_block, BI): acc_s_ub[h_i, j] = acc_s_ub[h_i, j] - m_i[h_i] ``` Here is some examples: - [MatmulAddDeveloper](./examples/developer_mode/matmul_add_developer.py) - [SparseFlashAttnDeveloperVidReduce](./examples/developer_mode/sparse_flash_attn_developer_vid_reduce.py) For a more detailed feature introduction, please see: - [vid_reduction_and_auto_cv_ratio.md](./docs/tutorials/vid_reduction_and_auto_cv_ratio.md) ### Workspace reduction Workspace Reduction is **automatically enabled** in the compilation pipeline. No manual configuration required. It automates workspace allocation for cross-core data transfer (L0C → UB), eliminating the need for users to manually write two-stage GM copy scripts and manage workspace buffers. ```python @T.prim_func def flash_attn(...): with T.Kernel(..., threads=2, is_npu=True) as (cid): # Cube computation T.gemm_v0(q_l1, k_l1, acc_s_l0c, transpose_B=True, init=True) # Single copy statement — Workspace Reduction automatically handles GM transfer T.copy(acc_s_l0c, acc_s_ub) # Vector computation T.tile.exp(acc_s_ub, acc_s_ub) T.reduce_max(acc_s_ub, m_i, dim=-1) T.tile.sub(acc_s_ub, acc_s_ub, m_i) ``` Here are some examples: - [FlashAttnDeveloper](./examples/developer_mode/flash_attn_bshd_developer.py) For a more detailed feature introduction, please see: - [workspace_reduction_tutorial.md](./docs/tutorials/workspace_reduction_tutorial.md) ## Contributing We welcome contributions of new operators and framework improvements! Please follow the guidelines below to ensure your changes integrate smoothly. ### Contributing Operators When adding a new operator: 1. Create your operator under the `examples/` directory (e.g., `examples/my_op/my_op.py`). 2. Make sure your script prints `Kernel Output Match!` or `Test Passed!` upon success, so the CI can recognize it. 3. Verify that `bench_test.sh` can discover and run your script — it auto-discovers `*.py` files up to 2 levels deep under `examples/`. 4. Run the full test suite locally before submitting: ```bash cd examples bash bench_test.sh ``` ### Contributing Framework Changes When modifying the compiler, passes, or runtime: 1. Ensure **all existing tests pass** by running `bench_test.sh` end-to-end. Framework changes must not break any existing operator. 2. The CI will also run `pytest` on `testing/python/` — make sure those tests pass as well. 3. If your change adds a new API or primitive, add corresponding test coverage under `testing/python/` or a new example under `examples/`. ### CI Overview The current CI workflow is triggered manually via [`bench_test.sh`](./examples/bench_test.sh). > **Rule of thumb**: If you add an operator, make sure `bench_test.sh` picks it up. If you change the framework, make sure `bench_test.sh` still reports 100% pass. ## Upcoming Features Check our [tilelang-ascend development plan](https://github.com/tile-ai/tilelang-ascend/issues/3) for upcoming features. ## Acknowledgements We gratefully acknowledge the valuable support provided by Huawei's HiSilicon, ICT, Compiler and Programming Language Lab and the Peking University Kunpeng & Ascend Center for Excellence in Science, Education, and Innovation.

content.content:
1	# TileLang-Ascend Programming Guide
2	
3	## 1. TileLang介绍
4	
5	TileLang是一种面向tile（数据块）级别编程的DSL（领域特定语言），基于其数据块层级的抽象，使开发者能够以一种高级、可组合的方式表达和优化底层内核行为。TileLang可以让开发者显式控制内存分配、数据移动、布局和并行执行。
6	
7	下图展示了TileLang程序如何从高级描述逐步降低为面向特定硬件的可执行程序。我们提供了三种不同的编程接口，分别面向初学者、开发者和专家用户，这些接口分别位于这一降低流程的不同层级。TileLang还允许在同一内核中混合使用这些接口，使用户能够根据自身需求选择最适合的抽象层次进行编程。
8	
9	![image-tilelang_ascend_mode](./images/image-tilelang_ascend_mode.png)
10	
11	- **Beginner Level (Hardware-Unaware)**
12	
13	  这种模式主要适用于需要编写不依赖于特定硬件细节代码的用户，目标是让开发者能够专注于基本逻辑，而不必担心内存层次结构或硬件特定的优化。
14	
15	  > 当前还不支持该编程模式。
16	
17	- **Developer Level (Hardware-Aware with Tile Library)**
18	
19	  专为对AI芯片内存层次结构和性能考量有基本了解的开发人员设计，提供了一个Tile库，其中包含针对各种硬件架构优化的预定义操作和模式。这一级别的用户可以利用这些现成的原语，而无需深入研究底层的线程细节。
20	
21	- **Expert Level (Hardware-Aware with Thread Primitives)**
22	
23	  对于那些对底层硬件特性（例如Ascend的Cube、Vector、MTE、Unified Buffer等）有深入理解的高经验用户而言，提供了更底层的硬件控制，如细粒度同步、更低级别的操作接口和寄存器相关的设置等，从而能够对性能关键的内核代码进行细粒度的控制。这一层级为针对特定架构的专门优化提供了最大的灵活性。
24	
25	## 2. TileLang开发快速入门
26	
27	### 2.1 TileLang开发环境
28	
29	第一步，**CANN环境准备**：
30	
31	我们假设您已搭建好包含CANN（至少8.3.RC1版本）和torch-npu（至少2.6.0.RC1版本）的昇腾环境，首先设置CANN环境变量。
32	
33	```
34	source {your-cann-installed-path}/ascend-toolkit/set_env.sh
35	```
36	
37	第二步是**安装TileLang-Ascend**，我们这里采用源码安装的方式：
38	
39	```
40	a) 下载
41	git clone --recursive https://github.com/tile-ai/tilelang-ascend.git
42	cd tilelang-ascend
43	
44	b) 编译安装
45	bash install_ascend.sh
46	
47	c) 设置环境变量
48	source set_env.sh
49	```
50	
51	然后，就可以**运行**examples下面的例子：
52	
53	```
54	cd examples/gemm
55	python example_gemm.py
56	
57	成功后会打印：
58	Kernel Output Match!
59	```
60	
61	### 2.2 TileLang 算子kernel示例
62	
63	下面是一个TileLang开发的kernel函数示例，实现两个张量做逐元素和（Elementwise Add）：
64	
65	```python
66	import tilelang
67	import tilelang.language as T
68	from tilelang import jit
69	
70	import torch
71	
72	pass_configs = {
73	    tilelang.PassConfigKey.TL_ASCEND_AUTO_SYNC: True,
74	    tilelang.PassConfigKey.TL_ASCEND_MEMORY_PLANNING: True,
75	}
76	
77	M = 1024
78	N = 1024
79	block_M = 128
80	block_N = 128
81	
82	VEC_NUM = 2
83	
84	@jit(out_idx=[-1], pass_configs=pass_configs)
85	def tile_add(M: int, N: int, block_M: int, block_N: int, dtype: str = 'float'):
86	    m_num = M // block_M
87	    n_num = N // block_N
88	
89	    @T.prim_func
90	    def add_kernel(
91	        A: T.Tensor((M, N), dtype),
92	        B: T.Tensor((M, N), dtype),
93	        C: T.Tensor((M, N), dtype),
94	    ):
95	        with T.Kernel(m_num * n_num, is_npu=True) as (cid, vid):
96	            bx = cid // n_num
97	            by = cid % n_num
98	
99	            a_ub = T.alloc_shared((block_M // VEC_NUM, block_N), dtype)
100	            b_ub = T.alloc_shared((block_M // VEC_NUM, block_N), dtype)
101	            c_ub = T.alloc_shared((block_M // VEC_NUM, block_N), dtype)
102	            
103	            T.copy(A[bx * block_M + vid * block_M // VEC_NUM, by * block_N], a_ub)
104	            T.copy(B[bx * block_M + vid * block_M // VEC_NUM, by * block_N], b_ub)
105	
106	            for i, j in T.Parallel(block_M // VEC_NUM, block_N):
107	                c_ub[i, j] = a_ub[i, j] + b_ub[i, j]
108	
109	            T.copy(c_ub, C[bx * block_M + vid * block_M // VEC_NUM, by * block_N])
110	
111	    return add_kernel
112	
113	func = tile_add(M, N, block_M, block_N)
114	
115	torch.manual_seed(0)
116	
117	a = torch.randn(M, N).npu()
118	b = torch.randn(M, N).npu()
119	
120	torch.npu.synchronize()
121	print("init successful!")
122	
123	c = func(a, b)
124	
125	ref_c = a + b
126	
127	torch.testing.assert_close(c, ref_c, rtol=1e-2, atol=1e-2)
128	print("Kernel Output Match!")
129	
130	```
131	
132	下面来看一下上面示例代码中的关键语法组成。
133	
134	首先是导入相关的库，然后就可以调用TileLang提供的功能：
135	
136	```python
137	import tilelang
138	import tilelang.language as T
139	from tilelang import jit
140	```
141	
142	接下来是算子kernel函数的定义和实现，TileLang算子kernel函数由`@T.prim_func` 装饰器在模块内定义（`add_kernel`），这部分会被TileLang调用编译工具链编译成可以在NPU上运行的二进制代码。Python函数`tile_add`包装了kernel函数，通过`return add_kernel`语句返回装饰过的`add_kernel`，供后续调用。
143	
144	```python
145	func = tile_add(M, N, block_M, block_N)
146	c= func(a, b)
147	```
148	
149	然后，我们来看下kernel内部的部分。
150	
151	`T.Tensor`将kernel的参数（`A`、`B`、`C`）声明为张量数据类型，其中通过`@jit`装饰器的参数out_idx=[-1]来指定最后一个参数、也即`C`为输出参数，其余参数为输入参数（关于`@jit`后续会详细说明，可以理解为调用被其装饰的函数时会触发即时编译）。
152	
153	`T.Kernel`原语定义了一个kernel运行的上下文。在其中，通过调用TileLang提供的各种内存分配（`T.alloc_shared`）、数据搬运（`T.copy`）、计算原语（如上述被`T.Parallel`包围的计算逻辑）实现算子逻辑。
154	
155	VEC_NUM用来指定vector计算单元的数量。由于在Ascend架构中，每个AI Core中有两个Vector计算单元，所以针对每个切分后的Tile，还可以进一步切分为两个sub tile，充分利用vector计算资源。
156	
157	
158	
159	还有一部分是数据切分逻辑。待计算数据是`(M, N)`大小的数据，由于片上存储空间的限制，需要进行切分成多个能够容纳的Tile块，并且通过并行计算。例如，上面的代码中，`(block_M, block_N)`就是切分的Tile的大小，可以图示如下：
160	
161	![image-tilelang_ascend_demo_tile](./images/image-tilelang_ascend_demo_tile.png)
162	
163	这个切分的Tile的数量为`m_num * n_num`，上述的`T.kernel`可以理解为为切分后的每个Tile创建一个并发执行单元，kernel里定义的操作在每个Tile上执行搬运、计算，多个并发执行单元并发运行，互不影响。`with T.kernel`返回的元组`(cid, vid)`中，`cid`可以理解为计算任务的数量（每个Tile对应一个计算任务，对应一个逻辑核来处理），`vid`值为0、1，即每个Tile再由两个子计算单元来完成。
164	
165	
166	
167	示例代码中的其余部分是通过调用torch来实现参考值，然后和算子计算输出的实际值进行比对，以验证算子逻辑的正确性。
168	
169	### 2.3 TileLang编译和运行
170	
171	TileLang Ascend的工作流程，主要分为编译和运行两个阶段：
172	
173	![image-tilelang_ascend_compile_run](./images/image-tilelang_ascend_compile_run.png)
174	
175	- 编译阶段
176	  1. 多轮lower转换：TileLang算子代码根据NPU硬件特性进行多级降级，生成针对昇腾硬件优化的TensorIR表示
177	  2. AscendC代码生成：基于TensorIR，使用专门的Ascend Codegen模块生成对应的AscendC代码
178	  3. 动态库编译：通过毕昇编译器（bisheng）将AscendC代码编译成动态链接库（.so文件）
179	- 运行阶段
180	  1. 库文件加载：通过ctypes将.so文件加载到Python环境中
181	  2. 函数封装：将算子封装为可调用的Python函数对象
182	  3. 执行调用：用户以普通Python函数方式调用，提供输入张量即可在昇腾NPU上执行计算并获得结果
183	
184	
185	
186	TileLang还支持JIT（Just-in-time，即时编译）。JIT是一种动态编译技术，Tilelang算子开发过程中通过JIT调用CodeGen生成AscendC代码，并对整个过程进行动态调控，解决静态编译的局限性，确保生成的AscendC代码动态适配NPU特性，同时最大化提升算子执行效率。
187	
188	- 动态参数驱动的AscendC定制代码生成。JIT会在运行中实时解析输入参数，同步向CodeGen传递参数维度、数据类型等信息，确保NPU算子支持动态输入。
189	- NPU硬件约束下的AscendC语法修正。JIT在运行时可检测当前NPU硬件的资源配置，严格遵守硬件资源限制，指导CodeGen生成符合性能约束的AscendC代码。
190	- 算子运行时的即时编译与动态优化。算子运行过程中，JIT会在编译过程中结合NPU当前的硬件状态优化指令分配，根据AI Core的利用率和内存占用情况动态调整编译策略。
191	
192	在TileLang kernel开发中，通过 **@jit** 装饰器来触发调用时的即时编译。
193	
194	### 2.4 A5 Camodel 仿真运行
195	
196	如果需要在 **无真实 A5 NPU 硬件** 的环境下开发和验证 A5 kernel，可以使用 CANN 提供的 **camodel（Cycle-Accurate Model，节拍精确模型）** 进行软件仿真。只要安装了包含 A5 simulator 镜像（`Ascend950PR_9599`）的 CANN 包，即可在任意 x86/Linux 机器上模拟 A5 平台运行 TileLang kernel，完成正确性验证和指令级分析。
197	
198	#### 2.4.1 为什么需要 camodel 仿真
199	
200	- **无 NPU 硬件时开发和验证**：在只有 CPU 的服务器或开发机上运行和调试 kernel
201	- **指令级 trace 分析**：camodel 可以输出每个 AIC core 的指令日志（`core*.instr_log.dump`）、UB 读写 dump（`core*.ub.rd_log.dump`/`core*.ub.wr_log.dump`），用于分析 kernel 执行细节
202	- **快速迭代**：不需要排队等待 NPU 资源，本地即可验证 kernel 逻辑正确性
203	
204	#### 2.4.2 原理
205	
206	原始 kernel 运行流程：`DSL 定义 → JIT 编译 → torch.npu 分配 NPU 内存 → 真实 NPU 执行`
207	
208	camodel 仿真流程：`DSL 定义 → 链接 libruntime_camodel.so 编译 → rtMalloc 分配模拟内存 → CPU 模拟 NPU 执行`
209	
210	核心区别在于编译时**用 `libruntime_camodel.so` 替代 `libruntime.so`**——前者是一个用软件模拟 NPU 行为的库，对外接口与真实运行时库完全一致。
211	
212	#### 2.4.3 一条命令运行内置示例
213	
214	TileLang-Ascend 提供了开箱即用的仿真运行脚本，位于 `.agents/skills/tilelang-a5-sim-convert/` 目录下。运行前需要确保基础环境已就绪（CANN 已安装、`bisheng` 编译器可用、`tilelang` 可 import）。脚本会自动完成 camodel 相关的环境设置（库路径、设备初始化、`os.execve` 重启等），无需手动配置 `TL_RUN_MODE`、`LD_LIBRARY_PATH` 等仿真专用变量：
215	
216	```bash
217	python .agents/skills/tilelang-a5-sim-convert/scripts/run_a5_sim_template.py
218	```
219	
220	成功输出：
221	```
222	KERNEL OUTPUT MATCH!
223	Done!
224	```
225	
226	脚本会自动完成：查找 CANN 安装路径 → 设置 camodel 库路径 → 加载软件模拟 NPU → 编译 kernel → 分配模拟内存 → 启动 kernel → 验证结果。
227	
228	可通过 `--log-dir` 指定 camodel 日志输出目录：
229	
230	```bash
231	python .agents/skills/tilelang-a5-sim-convert/scripts/run_a5_sim_template.py --log-dir ./my_sim_logs
232	```
233	
234	#### 2.4.4 将已有脚本转换为仿真版本
235	
236	使用 `/tilelang-a5-sim-convert` skill（位于 `.agents/skills/tilelang-a5-sim-convert/`），输入一个 tilelang DSL 脚本路径，自动生成对应的 `*_sim.py` 仿真脚本（不覆盖原始文件）：
237	
238	```
239	/tilelang-a5-sim-convert examples/gemm/example_gemm.py
240	```
241	
242	转换的核心改动（人工转换时也遵循相同规则）：
243	
244	| 原始脚本 | 仿真脚本 |
245	|---------|---------|
246	| `import torch` | 删除（用 `numpy` 替代） |
247	| `torch.randn(...).half().npu()` | `np.zeros(...)` + `rtMalloc` + `rtMemcpy` |
248	| `@tilelang.jit(out_idx=[-1])` | `def make_kernel(): return main`（DSL 逻辑不变） |
249	| `T.Tensor((M, K), dtype)` | `T.Tensor((1024, 256), "float16")`（替换为具体数值） |
250	| `T.alloc_L0C(..., "float16")` | `T.alloc_L0C(..., "float")`（A5 pto-isa 要求 float32 累积器） |
251	| `c = func(a, b)` | `kl.call(d_A, d_B, d_C, stream)`（RT API 调用） |
252	| `torch.testing.assert_close` | `np.abs(got - ref).max()` |
253	
254	详细模板和逐行说明见 `.agents/skills/tilelang-a5-sim-convert/`。
255	
256	#### 2.4.5 环境变量说明
257	
258	仿真运行依赖以下环境变量（由 `run_a5_sim.py` 自动设置，手动运行时需自行配置）：
259	
260	| 变量 | 值 | 作用 |
261	|------|------|------|
262	| `TL_RUN_MODE` | `sim` | 触发 camodel 编译路径（替换 `-lruntime` → `-lruntime_camodel`） |
263	| `TL_PLATFORM` | `A5` | 指定目标平台（仅在 `TL_RUN_MODE=sim` 时生效，不影响真实 NPU 硬件检测） |
264	| `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` | 需在最前面包含 `<CANN>/tools/simulator/Ascend950PR_9599/lib` | 让动态链接器优先找到 camodel 库 |
265	| `TORCH_DEVICE_BACKEND_AUTOLOAD` | `0` | 阻止 `torch_npu` 自动初始化（camodel 环境下会失败） |
266	| `CAMODEL_LOG_PATH` | 任意目录路径 | camodel 日志输出目录（包含 instruction trace、UB dump 等） |
267	
268	#### 2.4.6 局限性
269	
270	- 仅支持 PTO 后端（`target="pto"`）的 A5 平台仿真
271	- camodel 模拟器的执行速度远慢于真实 NPU（约 1000 倍以上），仅适用于功能验证，不适用于性能测试
272	- 不支持 `torch.npu` 接口，数据管理需通过 `rtMalloc`/`rtMemcpy` 等 RT API
273	- 需要 CANN 9.0.0 及以上版本（包含 `Ascend950PR_9599` simulator 镜像）
274	
275	---
276	
277	## 3. TileLang语法基础
278	
279	本节介绍TileLang（tile-lang）领域特定语言（DSL）的核心语法基础，你将使用这种语言编写高性能的内核。重点介绍如何定义内核、表达迭代操作、在内存域之间移动数据，以及如何通过即时编译（JIT）运行内核。
280	
281	### 3.1 kernel定义
282	
283	TileLang kernel是基于TIR（TVM IR）生成的函数，用`@T.prim_func`来修饰。参数类型为`T.Tensor`或`T.Buffer`，包含了shape和dtype信息。
284	
285	```
286	@T.prim_func
287	def add_kernel(
288	    A: T.Tensor((N,), dtype),    # dtype could be 'float32'
289	    B: T.Tensor((N,), dtype),
290	    C: T.Tensor((N,), dtype),
291	):
292	    ...  # kernel body
293	```
294	
295	shape除了可以是整形常量外，还可以是符号变量的形式表示，以支持动态信息传递。在TileLang中，支持两种符号变量的形式：
296	
297	- **T.dyn[...]**
298	
299	  这种方式对于符号变量的使用，在kernel体内通过buffer的shape信息来获取和使用。
300	
301	  ```
302	  # 1) Annotation-only symbol; read the bound size via shape
303	  K = T.dyn['K']  # dtype defaults to int32
304	  @T.prim_func
305	  def foo(A: T.Tensor((K,), 'float32')):
306	      N = A.shape[0]
307	      for i in T.serial(N):
308	          ...
309	  ```
310	
311	  
312	
313	- **T.dynamic(name, dtype)**
314	
315	   这种方式创建一个tir.Var，然后可以直接在后续的表达式和循环语句中使用该符号。
316	
317	  ```
318	  # 2) Explicit Var symbol usable in the body
319	  K = T.dynamic('K', 'int32')   # or T.dynamic('K') defaults to int32
320	  @T.prim_func
321	  def bar(A: T.Tensor((K,), 'float32')):
322	      for i in T.serial(K):
323	          ...
324	  ```
325	
326	注意：
327	
328	- T.symbolic(name, dtype) 是T.dynamic的一个已弃用的别名；建议使用T.dynamic。
329	- 在 `@jit`中, 具体的尺寸来自第一次调用时传入的实际张量参数.
330	- 注解中的符号不需要作为单独的kernel参数；TileLang 会从参数形状中绑定它们。
331	
332	### 3.2 数据类型
333	
334	dtype用于指定Tile的数据类型，支持的类型列表有：
335	
336	```
337	float16, float32, bfloat16, int8, int16, int32, int64, uint8, uint16, uint32, uint64
338	```
339	
340	
341	
342	### 3.3 kernel launch
343	
344	**with T.Kernel(...)** 声明一个kernel运行上下文，并且创建数据tile block与逻辑核的绑定关系。对于Ascend NPU来说，对于每个block，返回一个（cid，vid)的元组。cid的范围为 [0,block_num), vid的范围为0或1。因为A2/A3的CV核配比可以为1:2或1:1, 可以通过vid指定当前vector的索引。
345	
346	下面的代码片段对于(M, N)大小的数据块，切分为（block_M，block_N）大小的基本tile block，tile block的数量为m_num * n_num个，代码逻辑可以理解为多个并发的执行单元，每个单元处理一个tile block（针对每个tile block，又可以根据vector数量切分为1个或2个vector单元并发处理）。
347	
348	```
349	m_num = M // block_M
350	n_num = N // block_N
351	VEC_NUM = 2
352	
353	@T.prim_func
354	def main(A: T.Tensor((M, N), dtype),
355	         B: T.Tensor((M, N), dtype),
356	         C: T.Tensor((M, N), dtype)):
357	    with T.Kernel(m_num * n_num, is_npu=True) as (cid, vid):
358	        ......
359	```
360	
361	
362	
363	### 3.4 Loops和Control Flow
364	
365	TileLang kernel支持标准Python语法中的if/elif/else条件语句。条件应该是TIR expression（例如：i < N），Python中的普通布尔值被视为编译时常量，并且会被折叠（即优化掉）。
366	
367	```
368	for i in T.serial(N):
369	    if i < N:            # TIR condition
370	        C[i] = A[i] + B[i]
371	    else:
372	        pass
373	
374	# Ternary
375	x = (A[i] if i < N else 0)
376	```
377	
378	
379	
380	TileLang支持多种循环表达形式。
381	
382	- **Serial**
383	
384	**T.serial**构造普通的for循环。
385	
386	```
387	for i in T.serial(N):
388	    ...                     # 0..N-1
389	
390	for i in T.serial(0, N, 2):
391	    ...                     # 0, 2, 4, ...
392	```
393	
394	- **Unroll**
395	
396	**T.unroll**针对小循环次数进行循环展开。
397	
398	```
399	for k in T.unroll(K_TILE):
400	    acc += a[k] * b[k]
401	```
402	
403	这是一种高级使用模式，TileLang 将展开提示传递给 TIR；专家用户可通过因子化或显式调节参数进行优化调优。
404	
405	- **Parallel**（element-wise）
406	
407	**T.Parallel**(ext0, ext1, ...)构建嵌套循环，这些循环能够很好地将Tile运算映射到逐元素操作。循环体通过一个for头接收所有索引：
408	
409	- **运算操作**：
410	```python
411	# 一维运算场景
412	for i in T.Parallel(v_block):
413	    m_i[i] = T.max(m_i[i], m_i_prev[i])
414	```
415	```python
416	# 二维运算场景
417	for (i, j) in T.Parallel(v_block, d):
418		acc_o_ub[i, j] /= T.exp(attn_sink_ub[i] - scores_max[i])
419	```
420	- **拷贝操作**：
421	
422	``` python
423	# GM -> UB 拷贝&计算场景
424	for i, j in T.Parallel(block_M // VEC_NUM, block_N):
425		C[bx * block_M + vid * block_M // VEC_NUM + i, by * block_N + j] = T.exp(a_ub[i, j])
426	```
427	
428	Developer模式调度原语章节会有详细介绍。
429	
430	- **Pipelined**
431	
432	**T.Pipelined**(iters, num_stages=...)可以进行计算/搬运的流水掩盖。
433	
434	```
435	for ko in T.Pipelined(T.ceildiv(K, BK), num_stages=3):
436	    T.copy(A[by * BM, ko * BK], A_s)   # stage: copy A tile
437	    T.copy(B[ko * BK, bx * BN], B_s)   # stage: copy B tile
438	    T.gemm_v0(A_s, B_s, C_f)           # stage: compute
439	```
440	三段式流水并行排布示意：
441	```
442	------------------------------------->
443	  stage1  |     stage2     |  stage3 
444	--------------------------------------
445	copy copy | copy copy copy | ---- ----
446	---- ---- | gemm gemm gemm | gemm gemm
447	--------------------------------------
448	```
449	
450	Developer模式调度原语章节会有详细介绍。
451	
452	- **Persistent**
453	
454	**T.Persistent**(domain, wave_size, index, group_size=...)可以让数据在多个AI Core间负载更均衡，并且提高数据缓存的命中概率。
455	
456	```
457	for bx, by in T.Persistent([T.ceildiv(M, block_M), T.ceildiv(N, block_N)],
458	                    core_num, cid):
459	    ...
460	```
461	
462	- **While loop**
463	
464	TileLang支持while循环表达，循环条件需要是TIR expression。如果TileLang检测出死循环会编译报错。
465	
466	```
467	i = 0
468	while i < N:
469	    ...
470	    if done:
471	        break
472	    i += 1
473	```
474	
475	
476	
477	**Break和Continue**
478	
479	在T.serial/T.unroll/T.Parallel/while循环中，可以使用break/continue来退出整个循环或本次循环。
480	
481	## 4. TileLang编程模式和原语
482	
483	### 4.1 Developer模式
484	
485	Developer编程模式主要是基于TileLang定义的Tile Library接口以及原语来编写TileLang kernel，开发者基于这种开发方式会更容易，而且代码层面理论上也可以做到跨架构平台的兼容。当然，基于Develoer模式，也可以调用Expert模式的扩展接口，这通常是为了性能考虑。
486	
487	#### 4.1.1 内存分配原语
488	
489	TileLang中可以显示指定存储的分配层级，并且对存储层级进行了抽象，分为Global、shared和fragment级别，这里的内存分配主要关注片上存储。
490	
491	![image-tilelang_ascend_memory](./images/image-tilelang_ascend_memory.png)
492	
493	其中，shared层级对应的存储位于片上的高速存储，该层级的存储常用于缓存计算过程中的临时中间数据，因为它的访问速度要远高于Global Memory（HBM）。例如，在矩阵计算时，经过切分的tile粒度的小数据块可以被首先加载到shared层级的内存，后续的操作都直接访问shared内存，从而减少频繁的从Global Memory加载和存储带来的性能开销。
494	
495	fragment层级的存储对应偏上的寄存器级别的存储单元，一般用于某一个计算单元（例如Cube）的输入和输出，该层级的存储容量一般较小，但访问速度要最快，要高于shared层级的存储。例如，在矩阵计算时，左矩阵和右矩阵分别被加载到对应的fragment层级的存储，计算后的结果也存储到fragment层级的存储，从而实现高效的矩阵计算。
496	
497	两个层级的存储分配定义如下。
498	
499	- `T.alloc_shared(shape, dtype)`: 
500	
501	  **参数**：
502	
503	  - Parameters:
504	
505	    **shape** (*tuple*) – The shape of the buffer to allocate 
506	
507	    **dtype** (*str*) – The data type of the buffer (e.g., ‘float32’, ‘int32’)
508	
509	  **功能说明**：分配shared类型的存储空间。
510	
511	  **举例**：
512	
513	  ```
514	  A_L1 = T.alloc_shared((block_M, block_K), dtype)
515	  ```
516	
517	- `T.alloc_fragment(shape, dtype, scope='local.fragment')`: 
518	
519	  **参数**：
520	
521	  - Parameters:
522	
523	    **shape** (*tuple*) – The shape of the buffer to allocate
524	
525	    **dtype** (*str*) – The data type of the buffer (e.g., ‘float32’, ‘int32’)
526	
527	  **功能说明**：分配fragment类型的存储空间。
528	
529	  **举例**：
530	
531	  ```
532	  C_L0 = T.alloc_fragment((block_M, block_N), accum_dtype)
533	  ```
534	
535	- `T.alloc_var(dtype, init, scope='local.var')`:
536	
537	  **参数**：
538	
539	  - **dtype** (*str*) – 变量的数据类型（例如：'float32', 'int32', 'bool'）
540	
541	  - **init** (*可选*) – 初始值，可以是常量值、表达式或其他变量
542	
543	  - **scope** (*str, 可选*) – 内存作用域，默认为 "local.var"
544	
545	  **功能说明**：
546	
547	  分配变量用于存储标量数据。适用于条件判断的标志位、循环计数器、临时标量变量等场景。支持灵活的初始化方式，可以指定初始值或从其他变量初始化。
548	
549	  **举例**：
550	
551	  基础用法：
552	  ```
553	  # 分配布尔类型标志位，初始化为False
554	  flag = T.alloc_var("bool", init=False)
555	  
556	  # 分配整数变量，初始化为1
557	  counter = T.alloc_var("int32", init=1)
558	  
559	  # 分配浮点数变量，初始化为0.0
560	  value = T.alloc_var("float32", init=0.0)
561	  ```
562	
563	  变量间初始化：
564	  ```
565	  # 用另一个变量的值初始化
566	  a = T.alloc_var("int32", init=1)
567	  b = T.alloc_var("int32", init=a)  # b的初始值为a的值
568	  ```
569	
570	  在条件逻辑中使用：
571	  ```
572	  flag = T.alloc_var("bool", init=False)
573	  a = T.alloc_var("int32", init=1)
574	  
575	  flag = True
576	  if flag:
577	      a = 2
578	  else:
579	      a = a + 1
580	  ```
581	
582	  指定内存作用域：
583	  ```
584	  # 使用默认作用域
585	  var1 = T.alloc_var("int32", init=1)
586	  
587	  # 显式指定作用域
588	  var2 = T.alloc_var("int32", "local.var", init=1)
589	  var3 = T.alloc_var("int32", init=1, scope="local.var")
590	  ```
591	
592	  **注意**：
593	
594	  - 初始化值会直接写入变量，而不是默认的零值
595	  - 支持的初始化值类型包括常量、表达式和其他变量
596	  
597	在Ascend平台中，shared层级的存储对应到L1 Buffer 和 Unified Buffer，前者用于Cube计算，后者对应到Vector计算。但用户无需关心指定的存储是L1 Buffer还是Unified Buffer，TileLang的编译器会通过程序上下文自动分析和识别。fragment层级的存储对应到L0A/L0B/L0C Buffer，同样，用户无需显示指定是分配的是哪种，TileLang编译器会根据程序上下文自动分析和识别。
598	
599	![image-tilelang_ascend_arch](./images/image-tilelang_ascend_arch.png)
600	
601	#### 4.1.2 数据搬运原语
602	
603	数据搬运操作可以实现tile数据块在不同的内存层级之间拷贝，支持tir.Buffer、BufferLoad、BufferRegion类型的数据。
604	
605	- `T.copy(src, dst)`:
606	
607	  **参数**：
608	
609	  Move tiles between Global/Shared/Fragment.
610	
611	  - Parameters:
612	
613	    **src**：源数据buffer
614	
615	    **dst**：目的数据buffer
616	
617	  **功能说明**：将数据从src搬运到dst所在的存储空间。
618	
619	  **举例**：
620	
621	  ```
622	  T.copy(A[bx * block_M, k * block_K], A_L1)
623	  ```
624	
625	支持的数据搬运类型有下标所示。
626	
627	| src  | dst  | 说明                                              |
628	| ---- | ---- | :------------------------------------------------ |
629	| GM   | L1   | 数据从Global Memory搬运到L1 Buffer                |
630	| L1   | L0A  | 数据从L1 Buffer搬运到L0A Buffer，Cube计算的左矩阵 |
631	| L1   | L0B  | 数据从L1 Buffer搬运到L0B Buffer，Cube计算的右矩阵 |
632	| L0C  | GM   | 数据从L0C Buffer搬运到Global Memory               |
633	| GM   | UB   | 数据从Global Memory搬运到Unified Buffer           |
634	| UB   | GM   | 数据从Unified Buffer搬运到Global Memory           |
635	| UB   | UB   | 数据从Unified Buffer搬运到Unified Buffer          |
636	| UB   | L1   | 数据从Unified Buffer搬运到L1 Buffer               |
637	
638	`T.tile.atomic_add(dst_gm, src_local)` 是 Ascend 专属的原子累加写回原语。它不是普通 `T.copy`，而是在 local tensor 到 GM 的写回过程中执行原子累加，适合多个 block/core 将 partial result 累加到同一 GM 输出的场景。若业务语义是从 0 开始累加，调用前或 kernel 内需要先清零 GM 输出。
639	
640	#### 4.1.3 计算原语
641	
642	##### 4.1.3.1 矩阵计算
643	
644	- `T.gemm_v0(A, B, C, transpose_A=False, transpose_B=False, init=False, kL0Size=128):`
645	
646	  **参数**：
647	
648	  - Parameters:
649	
650	    A：左输入矩阵
651	
652	    B：右输入矩阵
653	
654	    C：结果累加存储输出矩阵
655	
656	    transpose_A：是否要对A输入矩阵进行转置
657	
658	    transpose_B：是否要对B输入矩阵进行转置
659	
660	    init：在计算前下对累加矩阵C进行清零，一般情况下由于需要对矩阵进行切片，第一次计算需要对累加矩阵清零，后续在基础上累加。
661	
662	    kL0Size（高级参数，optional）：L1→L0 数据搬运时的 K 轴切分大小。控制 K 维度从 L1 搬到 L0A/L0B 时的切分粒度。必须是 16 的倍数，默认 128。通常不需要修改此参数。当 L0C 利用率不高（如 block_M × block_N × 4 < 128KB）或 kL0Size=128 导致 L0A/L0B 双缓冲溢出时，可以考虑调小 kL0Size。更小的 kL0Size 允许更大的 block_M/block_N（提高 L0C 利用率），代价是更多的 L1→L0 搬运次数。对于 half 精度，block_M=128, block_N=256 时推荐 kL0Size=64。
663	
664	  **功能说明**：gemm操作用来实现两个tile的矩阵乘操作，特别的是它的左矩阵（A_shared）和右矩阵（B_shared）都是位于shared存储层级，输出（C_fragment）位于fragment存储层级，A_shared和B_shared的进行矩阵乘操作，然后结果和C_fragment已有值进行累加并赋值到C_fragment。
665	
666	  ```
667	  C_fragment += A_shared * B_shared
668	  ```
669	
670	  **举例**：
671	
672	  ```
673	  for k in T.serial(loop_k):
674	      ......
675	      T.gemm_v0(A_L1, B_L1, C_L0, init=(k == 0))
676	      ......
677	  ```
678	  
679	
680	##### 4.1.3.2 Reduce类
681	
682	当前 Ascend reduce 仍然属于 fast-path 原语，主要服务于 UB tile / slice buffer 场景。本次接口语义与实现边界如下：
683	
684	- 当前支持 1D buffer、2D buffer，以及 3D trailing-tile buffer；当前主要验收范围是 2D UB/slice reduce。
685	- `dim` 支持范围：
686	  - 1D buffer：`0` / `-1`
687	  - 2D buffer：`0` / `1` / `-1` / `-2`
688	  - 3D buffer：仅支持 trailing-tile 轴 `0` / `1` / `-1` / `-2`
689	- `clear=True` 表示先初始化输出再写入 reduce 结果；`clear=False` 表示在已有 `out` 上做 merge：
690	  - `reduce_sum`：将 reduce 结果与已有 `out` 相加
691	  - `reduce_max`：将 reduce 结果与已有 `out` 逐元素取最大值
692	  - `reduce_min`：将 reduce 结果与已有 `out` 逐元素取最小值
693	- `real_shape` 用于描述 2D slice buffer 的逻辑有效区域；未设置时默认使用物理 buffer 形状。
694	- `out` 一般可以使用两类 shape：
695	  - 压缩后的 reduce 结果 shape。例如输入为 `[M, N]` 时，`dim=-1` 可输出为 `[M]`，`dim=0` 可输出为 `[N]`。
696	  - keepdim 形式的 shape，即保留被规约的轴，但该轴长度变为 `1`。例如输入为 `[M, N]` 时，`dim=-1` 可输出为 `[M, 1]`，`dim=0` 可输出为 `[1, N]`。
697	- `keepdim` 不表示输出 shape 可以任意保持为与输入 buffer 相同的 shape；只有在被规约轴本身长度就是 `1` 的退化情况下，数值上才可能与输入 shape 一致。
698	- 对 2D slice buffer 且设置了 `real_shape` 的兼容路径，`out` 还允许保持部分 physical-layout 形式，例如 `[physical_cols]` 或 `[1, physical_cols]`；这是为了兼容当前后端对 slice buffer 的 lowering 方式。
699	- 非法 `dim`、非法 `real_shape`、非法 `out` shape 会在前端直接报错，而不是静默进入后端。
700	- `clear` 和 `real_shape` 同时支持关键字传参和兼容的 positional 传参形式，建议优先使用关键字形式以获得更清晰的可读性。
701	
702	- `T.reduce_sum(buffer: Buffer, out: Buffer, dim: int = -1, clear: bool = True, real_shape: list[int] | None = None)`
703	
704	  **参数**：
705
